The Subject Collection

- For every dataset, there is one and only one subject collection as defined in Dataset.root_collection.

Subcollections

- Every subcollection has a direct relationship to the subject collection. It will be 1:many or many:may depending on the booean value of Collection.many_to_many_with_subject.

- A collection can be turned into a "point event" by defining Collection.event_date_field. This allows longitudinal queries on the collection.

- A collection can be turned into an "interval event" by also defining Collection.event_end_date_field. This allows longitudinal queries on the collection.

Subcollection Relationships

- Subcollections will always have a many:many relationship to each other through the subject collection. But if subcollections have a more precise direct relationship (ex. procedures are performed during a specific encounter) it is good to define that relationship as well.

- Those relationships are defined in the CollectionRelationship table. You need a shared concept in both tables (like an encounter ID) to define the relationship. The primary key concept can never be multivalue. If the foreign key concept is multivalue, it will be a many:many relationship. If it isn't multivalue, it will be a 1:many relationship.
